concerns.text: FR-007 mandates MARTINI (coarse-grained) 'or reduced system size' for runtime. MARTINI diffusion coefficients are known to be systematically faster than experimental values (CG time mapping is not 1:1), so MAE vs. experimental NIST values would be dominated by a force-field systematic offset, not by simulation timescale — the study's independent variable. The idea/plan specified atomistic OPLS-AA/GROMOS; switching to MARTINI undermines the research question. The 'D_scaled' field in Data Models suggests a scaling correction, but no FR/SC defines how scaling is derived or validated — as written, the timescale-accuracy curve could be an artifact of CG mapping.

R² ≥ 0.95 on MSD vs. time is a weak linearity diagnostic: R² is insensitive to curvature and, for 1 ns runs, a high R² can coexist with a ballistic-to-diffusive crossover that biases the slope. Standard practice is a log-log local-slope check (slope ≈ 1) or fitting only the late-time diffusive window. The spec should specify the fit window (e.g., discard the ballistic regime) rather than rely on R² alone.

With N=3 solvents, bootstrap CIs on MAE and a 'CI overlap check' between 1 ns and 10 ns have very low power; the spec correctly drops the p-value test, but the CI-overlap criterion is itself a conservative/noisy inference rule. State explicitly that conclusions are descriptive per-solvent, and consider per-solvent stratified reporting (which Principle VII partially mandates) so the N=3 aggregation is not the sole evidence.
